To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
diary completion and anagram solving reduce impact bias in judgments about future affect.

(1) people overestimate their affect associated with future events and decisions; (2) this is because they overestimate the duration of their affective reactions; (3) diary completion reduces impact bias; (4) this is because diary completers are distracted from the focal affective reaction, and not because diary completion changes the way people think about the focal affective reactions.
completing a diary or solving anagrams de-biases people's affective reactions to past and future events and that monitoring moods has the same effect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the impact bias is caused by a distraction or by a task interference.
the question of whether people are aware of the factors that influence their affective reactions.
the question of whether the impact bias can be reduced in judgments of post decisional affect by distracting people from the focal event.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the diary completion method de-biases impact bias by distracting participants from the focal event, and that the anagram completion method de-bias impact bias by interfering with processing.
diary completion and anagrams reduce the impact bias by distracting people and/or interfering with the cognitive processing required by judgments.
the impact bias is reduced by any task that interferes with the process of making the judgment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
people overestimate the affect associated with future and past events and decisions, and that this bias is due to an interference in the processing required for such judgments.
impact bias is reduced because diary completion distracts people from the event or because diary completion interfered with the processing required to make the judgment.
people overestimate their future affective reactions because they are distracted by the event itself, and that diary completion reduces impact bias because it distracts them from the event.
The main takeaway from our work is that
diary completion does not de-bias affective judgments by helping people to realize they will be distracted.
impact bias can be lowered by any task that interferes with the processes responsible for it, not only distraction.
the diary completion procedure is not a panacea.
